Subject: Acme RAG eval — retriever & reranker next steps

Hi Alex / Sara —

Great to chat this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Call highlights (from our discovery):
- Goal: replace current keyword-based answers with grounded answers for support and product docs.
- Corpus: ~120k internal docs (product guides, KB, release notes) + 10k customer emails.
- Constraints: p95 latency target < 600ms for user queries; grounding precision target >= 92%; limited budget for large-model inference.
- Success metrics: grounding precision (supporting evidence present), P@1, MRR, and hallucination rate.

Our recommended evaluation plan (shallow -> deep):
1) Pilot eval on 1k-doc sample + 200 representative queries from your team to validate retrieval settings and reranker choice.
2) Run end-to-end RAG eval (1k queries) with metrics: grounding precision, support rate, P@1, MRR, latency p95.
3) Iterate retriever (FAISS/HNSW params) and reranker (cross-encoder choice) to hit acceptance criteria.

Initial model recommendations:
- Embeddings/retriever: use open-embed-1024 (or your preferred embedding) + FAISS HNSW index; recall tuning at candidate_size=200 for the pilot.
- Reranker: cross-encoder (higher precision) for high-stakes answers. We can pilot both a lightweight bi-encoder reranker for cost comparison and a cross-encoder for quality.
- Generator: redwood-3b-gen-v1 (good latency/cost tradeoff) with conservative decoding parameters for grounding.

Attachments / resources I’m sharing: prompt_set_v1.txt (sample prompts + negative examples), acme_rag_benchmarks_20270601.csv (eval template), and a short benchmark primer: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/acme-rag-2027

Proposed next steps:
- Can you confirm a 1k-doc sample (randomly sampled) and 200-query set we should run against?
- If yes, we’ll kick off a 4-business-day pilot and share results + reranker recommendations.
- Schedule: Technical deep-dive with Michael to validate embedding choices and indexing pipeline. Suggested times: Wed/Thu next week — are you available?

If that all sounds good I’ll get the pilot scheduled and loop in engineering.

Thanks,
Marissa

Alex / Sara —
Looping Michael and Dev to propose a concrete eval configuration and include a quick cost/quality tradeoff. See below for proposed settings and acceptance criteria.

Proposed pilot config (1k-doc sample, 200 queries):
- Index: FAISS HNSW, M=32, efConstruction=200, efSearch=64
- Embeddings: open-embed-1024 (256k batch indexing)
- Retriever candidate_size: 200 (we can test 100/200/400 in sweep)
- Hybrid: BM25+vector hybrid scoring (to boost recall on short KB titles)
- Reranker options to evaluate:
  * cross-encoder-ranker-v2 (high-precision, higher latency/cost) — target P@1 uplift vs baseline
  * bi-encoder-reranker-lite (fast, lower cost) — target recall lift only

Evaluation metrics & definitions (used in CSV):
- grounding_precision: fraction of answers with at least one supporting doc cited correctly (>=1 doc).
- support_rate: percent of queries with any source returned.
- hallucination_rate: percent of answers with fabricated facts vs ground truth.
- P@1, MRR: standard ranking metrics.
- latency_p95: end-to-end p95 for production-config generator + reranker.

Acceptance criteria (for pilot to move to full eval):
- grounding_precision >= 92% OR a clear path (tuning + reranker) to reach it within 2 iterations.
- latency_p95 <= 600ms OR config that hits 600ms with a fallback to bi-encoder on high QPS.

Estimated timeline & deliverables:
- Day 0: confirm sample & queries (you)
- Day 1-2: index + run pilot sweep (our infra) — share acme_rag_benchmarks_20270601.csv populated with results
- Day 3: proposed reranker choice + tradeoffs (pdf attached)
- Day 4: next steps / rollout plan if criteria met

Cost notes (ballpark):
- Bi-encoder only: ~40-50% lower per-query cost vs cross-encoder (depends on candidate_size).
- Cross-encoder: higher CPU/GPU cost but often required to hit high grounding precision on short/ambiguous queries.

Please confirm the sample and the 200-query set; we’ll start indexing once you give the green light.

Thanks — looping Michael for the Thursday deep-dive at 10am PT.

Best,
Marissa

Alex — quick technical notes ahead of Thu’s call. Forwarding a short pilot summary we ran overnight on a 200-doc slice. See attached CSV for per-query metrics.

Summary & recommendation:
- Generator choice: redwood-3b-gen-v1 gives the best latency/cost balance. If you need higher knowledge fluency we can test open-llama-7b-instruct-quant but expect ~2x latency.
- Retriever: use FAISS HNSW hybrid with BM25 boost for titles. Candidate_size=200 is a good baseline; increase to 400 only if recall remains low after tuning.
- Reranker: cross-encoder-ranker-v2 recommended for production where grounding precision matters. If cost is a blocker, run bi-encoder-reranker-lite at inference and only cross-encode top-N (e.g., top 50) for a hybrid approach.

Pilot quick results (200-doc slice, 50 queries):
- grounding_precision: 89% (cross-encoder on candidate_size=100)
- support_rate: 94%
- hallucination_rate: 6%
- latency_p95 (cross-encoder + redwood-3b-gen-v1): ~680ms

Immediate tweaks I recommend before full pilot:
- Increase candidate_size -> 200 and enable BM25 hybrid to improve grounding_precision (expected +3-5%).
- Use selective cross-encode: bi-encoder first pass (cheap) -> cross-encode top 50. This should cut p95 ~20-30% vs cross-encoding all candidates.
- Cache frequent prefixes / query expansions for support flows to reduce repeated compute.

Attachments: acme_rag_benchmarks_20270601.csv (pilot results), reranker_proposal_v2.pdf (updated with pilot notes)

I’ll present these slides and the pilot table on Thu at 10am PT. If you want, we can run a quick extra sweep tonight with candidate_size=200 and return updated numbers by tomorrow morning.

- Michael
